Annual recertification required.

Founded 2005 by De Beers, Tiffany, Cartier, and 11 others. 2,000+ member companies globally across entire mine-to-retail supply chain. COP covers ethical, human rights, social, environmental practices. Three standards: COP, Chain of Custody (COC), Lab Grown Material Standard (LGMS). 2024 update adds DEI requirements. COP certification mandatory for all commercial members. PDF: https://www.responsiblejewellery.com/wp-content/uploads/RJC-2024-COP-Standard.pdf

codes.document_title: World Diamond Council System of Warranties (SoW)
codes.notes: Introduced January 2002 to complement Kimberley Process. Extends conflict-free assurance from rough to polished diamonds and jewelry. 2021 revision broadened to include human rights, labor rights, anti-corruption, anti-money laundering. Voluntary self-regulation with company registration and unique ID. Covers every time diamonds change hands.

codes.organization: Footwear Distributors and Retailers of America (FDRA)
codes.document_title: FDRA Footwear Production Code of Conduct
codes.notes: Founded 1944. Largest US footwear trade association, representing 95%+ of industry. Code based on 25+ company codes. Covers working hours, overtime, structural safety, transparency. Industry-wide standard for factory compliance. Endorsed by Wolverine Worldwide, Brown Shoe Company, R.G. Barry, BBC International, and others.

Founded 1999 from Apparel Industry Partnership (1996). International network of companies, universities, civil society. Ten Principles of Fair Labor and Responsible Sourcing. Covers: forced labor prohibition, child labor, harassment/abuse, nondiscrimination, health/safety, freedom of association, wages/benefits, working hours, regular employment, environment. ~75% of audited factories in apparel sector. PDF: https://www.fairlabor.org/wp-content/uploads/2022/09/21010-B_FLA_CodeOfConduct_Final.pdf

Founded 2000 by American Apparel and Footwear Association. World's largest independent certification for apparel, footwear, and sewn products. 12 Principles based on ILO conventions cover: child/forced labor, health/safety, harassment/abuse, discrimination, hours/compensation, freedom of association, environment, customs compliance, security. Accepted by Walmart, Disney, Costco, Kmart, Fruit of the Loom, and hundreds more.

codes.document_title: BRC Global Standard for Ethical Trade and Responsible Sourcing
codes.notes: UK trade association for retailers. Standard establishes criteria for sustainable management, supply chain transparency, and worker rights. Also developed Retailer Protocol for Modern Slavery cases. Additional BRC standards for food safety (est. 1998), now internationally recognized benchmarks. Now branded as BRCGS (BRC Global Standards).

Originally developed 2003, updated 2013 with expanded scope. Baseline in responsible sourcing for all sizes of Canadian retailers. References ILO conventions, best practice from NGOs and multilateral organizations. Responsible Sourcing Committee covers human rights, child labour, working conditions, trafficking, modern slavery, fair/living wages, worker safety.

subsectors.name: Sporting Goods, Hobby, Musical Instrument, Book, and Miscellaneous Retailers

codes.notes: Founded 1949. Strictest and most sweeping ethics code in the book trade. All members bound. Requires: authentic/accurately described material, full cash refund for misrepresented items, clear title passing, responsibility not to purchase/hold/resell stolen materials, not soliciting in other booksellers' premises. Rigorous membership screening beyond paying fees.

codes.document_title: ILAB Code of Usages and Customs
codes.notes: Defines universally recognized usages in antiquarian bookselling. Covers manuscripts, autographs, prints, maps, drawings, books, and all written/printed material. Requirements: accurate identification/description, clear pricing, 10% reciprocal trade discount to ILAB members, preservation of complete copies (no breaking intact books/manuscripts), scrupulous valuations. High ethical standards as basis of practice.

Founded 1999. Preserves traditional bookselling values in online context. Requirements: full business contact information, clear terms/conditions/return policies, accurate use of book trade terminology, clear/accurate descriptions, prompt shipping, fair return policies. Fosters mutual trust and respect between booksellers and customers.

Members commit to: honest/forthright transactions, service with integrity, maintaining professional/distinguished place of business, fair/vigorous competition to stimulate industry growth, obeying all local/state/federal laws and assisting prosecution of violators. Also: contributing to professional development, advocating pawnbroker rights, enhancing positive public image.

Fair and ethical principles for member companies in direct selling. Prohibits deceptive/false/unethical/unlawful consumer or recruiting practices. Each member designates a Code Responsibility Officer. Enforced by independent code administrator not connected to any member company with power to decide remedies. FTC copy available. PDF: https://www.dsa.org/docs/default-source/Code-of-Ethics/code-of-ethics.pdf

codes.organization: World Federation of Direct Selling Associations (WFDSA)
codes.notes: Founded 1978 by 12 DSAs. First World Code of Ethics established 1985. Covers: consumer protection, conduct towards direct sellers, prohibited practices, identification, cooling-off/returns, privacy, fairness, referral selling, delivery, recruiting, business information, remuneration, earnings claims, fees, loading, repurchase. All member DSAs must abide to extent consistent with local law.
Established 1956, revised 2020 for inclusivity. Covers safety, professional conduct, loyalty, leadership, integrity. Professional Standards Committee serves as guardian of the Code.
Applies to all IATA employees, subsidiaries, consultants, contractors, suppliers and business partners worldwide. Covers ethical conduct and social responsibilities.
Focuses on safety, public trust, and professional excellence. Actions represent the entire profession. Includes Professional Standards Program.
Anti-discrimination and harassment policy. Covers events, meetings, and professional interactions.
Prohibits officers from receiving compensation from corporate boards or personal payments from employers. Protects members' rights to assemble, vote, and participate.

codes.organization: American Institute of Aeronautics and Astronautics (AIAA)
codes.notes: Covers aerospace professionals broadly. Emphasizes public safety, rejection of bribery/fraud/corruption, crediting others' contributions, fair treatment. Ethics Committee handles violations.

codes.organization: American Association of Private Railroad Car Owners (AAPRCO)
codes.notes: Private railroad car owners. AAR (Association of American Railroads) focuses on technical standards rather than a formal ethics code. AREMA (American Railway Engineering and Maintenance-of-Way Association) is the other major body.

codes.document_title: Code of Ethics for IMO Personnel
codes.notes: UN specialized agency. Code covers integrity, accountability, discrimination, abuse of authority, harassment. Applies to IMO personnel and sets tone for maritime industry.
Voluntary code for maritime professionals worldwide (merchant/naval officers, pilots, Harbour Masters, surveyors, ship managers). Ethical considerations take precedence over commercial interests.

codes.organization: Society of Naval Architects and Marine Engineers (SNAME)
codes.notes: Follows Professional Engineers Code of Ethics. Covers confidentiality, conflicts of interest, improper solicitation, single-source compensation. Founded for naval architecture and marine engineering professionals.

codes.organization: American Trucking Associations (ATA) - Moving & Storage Conference
codes.document_title: ATA Moving & Storage Conference Code of Ethics
codes.notes: ATA Moving & Storage Conference division code. ATA is the largest national trade association for the trucking industry representing 37,000+ members.
Required for all TIA members and CTB (Certified Transportation Broker) certification. Covers fair dealing, honesty, integrity, professional conduct. Ethics Committee arbitrates disputes.
Active members must adhere to strict code. Covers truthful representation, accurate pricing, ethical/financial responsibility, professionalism, integrity.

codes.document_title: NTA Code of Ethics and Professional Responsibility
codes.notes: Requires respectful, professional treatment of all, inclusivity. Full code available at NTAonline.com.

subsectors.name: Pipeline Transportation
subsectors.notes: INGAA (Interstate Natural Gas Association of America) and API (American Petroleum Institute) are the main trade bodies. Neither has a prominently published standalone code of ethics for pipeline transportation specifically. API's ethics standards fall under the broader oil/gas sector (NAICS 21).

subsectors.name: Scenic and Sightseeing Transportation
subsectors.notes: Covered indirectly by USTOA and NTA codes under subsector 485. No dedicated scenic/sightseeing transportation ethics code found.

codes.organization: National Customs Brokers & Forwarders Association of America (NCBFAA)
codes.notes: Strict code for customs brokers, freight forwarders, NVOCCs, and ocean transportation intermediaries. Since 1897. 1,400+ member companies.

codes.organization: International Federation of Freight Forwarders Associations (FIATA)
codes.notes: Covers 40,000 forwarding/logistics firms, 10 million employees in 160 countries. Promotes integrity, transparency, compliance with international trade regulations.

codes.document_title: FAA Order 3750.7B - Ethical Conduct and Financial Disclosure
codes.notes: Regulatory code for FAA employees covering aviation support activities. Implements Ethics in Government Act. Covers financial disclosure and ethical conduct training.

codes.document_title: Standards of Ethical Conduct for USPS Employees (5 CFR 7001)
codes.notes: Supplemental standards of ethical conduct. Covers conflicts of interest, outside employment restrictions, misuse of position. Published in Federal Register 2023.

codes.document_title: Rules of Conduct for Postal Employees (39 CFR Part 447)
codes.notes: Federal regulations governing postal employee conduct. Covers gambling, misuse of position and time, Hatch Act restrictions on political activity.

codes.organization: Association of Couriers and Messageries of Quebec (ACMQ)
codes.notes: Founded 1994. Mission to enhance industry image through professional code of ethics. MCAA (Messenger Courier Association of the Americas) is the US/international body but no standalone ethics code found.

codes.document_title: IWLA Standards of Business Ethics (in Bylaws)
codes.notes: Since 1891. Bylaws promote high standard of business ethics for public/contract warehousing and warehouse logistics services. Only trade association for warehouse-based 3PL providers.

subsectors.name: Motion Picture and Sound Recording Industries

codes.organization: SAG-AFTRA (Screen Actors Guild-American Federation of Television and Radio Artists)
codes.document_title: SAG-AFTRA Code of Conduct on Sexual Harassment
codes.notes: Zero-tolerance policy against discrimination and harassment. Part of Four Pillars of Change initiative. Applies to all producers employing SAG-AFTRA members.

codes.document_title: Personal Manager Code of Ethics and Conduct
codes.notes: Governs ethical standards for relationship between performers and managers. Ensures conformity with applicable state laws.
Emphasizes integrity, honesty, professionalism. Includes set safety protocols developed with Hollywood Commission. Anti-harassment training program.

codes.document_title: WGA Code of Conduct / Community Standards
codes.notes: Covers safe, inclusive culture in writers' rooms and professional interactions. Includes Code of Working Rules prohibiting spec work. Agency Code of Conduct also published.

codes.organization: American Society of Business Publication Editors (ASBPE)
codes.notes: Updated February 2025. For business/trade/professional publications. Covers editorial independence, separation of advertising from editorial, transparency. Founded 1964.
Gold standard of aspirational journalism ethics codes. Four principles: seek truth, minimize harm, act independently, be accountable/transparent. First written 1973, revised 1984/1987/1996/2014.
For broadcast and digital journalists. Covers public obligation, error correction, conflicts of interest, editorial independence, diversity of sources. Includes separate Coverage Guidelines.

codes.document_title: Global Charter of Ethics for Journalists
codes.notes: Adopted June 2019 at 30th IFJ World Congress. 16 articles. Completes Bordeaux Declaration (1954). Endorsed by representatives of 500,000+ journalists worldwide.

codes.document_title: Code of Ethics for Visual Journalists
codes.notes: For photojournalists and visual journalists. Covers accuracy, resisting manipulation, avoiding stereotyping, treating subjects with dignity, special consideration for vulnerable subjects.

codes.document_title: ONA Social Newsgathering Ethics Code / Build Your Own Ethics Code
codes.notes: Innovative approach: Build Your Own Ethics Code tool for news organizations. Covers 40+ ethical issues including UGC, verification, data journalism, social networks. Also has Social Newsgathering Ethics Code.

codes.document_title: ASNE Statement of Principles (Canons of Journalism)
codes.notes: Originally 'Canons of Journalism' adopted 1922 — landmark document that became model for journalism codes globally. Covers responsibility, freedom of the press, independence, truth/accuracy, impartiality, fair play.

Voluntary code for wireless carriers. Covers service disclosure, mapping, device unlocking. Also has Messaging Principles and Best Practices (updated 2023) covering ethical messaging, opt-in consent, content prohibitions.

codes.document_title: ITU Standards of Conduct / Ethics Framework
codes.notes: UN specialized agency. Ethics Office promotes highest standards. Includes policies on harassment, fraud/corruption, whistleblowing, all updated June 2025. Standards of Conduct for International Civil Service.

codes.document_title: ISOC Code of Conduct for Individual Members / Board and Officer Code of Ethics
codes.notes: Three-tier ethics framework: Individual Members (2003), Board/Officers, and Staff (2015). Covers internet governance professionals. Values: integrity, openness, honesty.

subsectors.name: Computing Infrastructure Providers, Data Processing, Web Hosting

codes.document_title: ACM Code of Ethics and Professional Conduct
codes.notes: Gold standard for computing profession. Adopted June 2018 after two-year global consultation. Covers public good, harm avoidance, honesty, fairness, privacy, confidentiality. Applies to all computing professionals.

codes.organization: IEEE (Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers)
codes.notes: 10 rules covering public safety, competence, fair treatment, discrimination prevention, sustainable development, privacy. All IEEE members agree to abide. Also co-published Software Engineering Code of Ethics with ACM/IEEE-CS.

codes.organization: ISC2 (International Information System Security Certification Consortium)
codes.document_title: ISC2 Code of Ethics / Code of Professional Conduct
codes.notes: Four canons: protect society, act honorably, provide competent service, advance the profession. New Code of Professional Conduct launched Feb 2026 with input from 1,400 cybersecurity professionals. Mandatory for all CISSP holders.

codes.document_title: AITP Code of Ethics and Standards of Conduct
codes.notes: Founded 1951. Three obligations: to society (knowledge dissemination, privacy), to employers (faithful service), to fellow members (honesty, respect). Acquired by CompTIA in 2017, rebranded as CompTIA IT Pro.
Nine principles. Created 1939, most recent amendment 2021 added racial/social justice principle. Covers intellectual freedom, access to information, privacy, professional development, equity.

codes.organization: International Federation of Library Associations and Institutions (IFLA)
codes.document_title: IFLA Code of Ethics for Librarians and Other Information Workers
codes.notes: Approved August 2012. Available in long and short versions. Translated into many languages. Model for 60+ national library association codes. Covers access, privacy, confidentiality.

codes.document_title: SAA Core Values Statement and Code of Ethics
codes.notes: First adopted 1980, revised 1992/2005/2012/2020. Companion document with Core Values. Covers authenticity, integrity, access, privacy, culturally sensitive materials, professional relationships.

codes.organization: Association for Information Science and Technology (ASIS&T)
codes.document_title: ASIS&T Professional Guidelines / Code of Conduct
codes.notes: Covers obligations to employers, clients, system users, the profession, and society. Emphasizes awareness of social, economic, cultural, political impacts. Recently merged with SLA (Special Libraries Association).
For special/corporate librarians and information professionals. Merged with ASIS&T in 2025.

codes.document_title: Supplemental Standards of Ethical Conduct for Employees of the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
codes.notes: 5 CFR Part 8101. Supplements OGE Standards of Ethical Conduct.

codes.document_title: Code of Conduct for Senior Financial Officers and Additional Policies on Ethics and Conflicts of Interest
codes.notes: Post-2021 trading scandal reforms. Restricts individual stock trading.

codes.notes: BIS organizational code covering independence, conflicts of interest, confidentiality.
Covers trust, integrity, fair dealing. Over 4,000 member institutions.
Community banking sector ethics.

codes.notes: Residential and commercial mortgage lending.

codes.notes: Ethics for mortgage brokers and loan originators.

codes.notes: CUNA merged with NAFCU in 2024. Cooperative ethics.

codes.notes: Syndicated loan market conduct standards.

Factoring and accounts receivable finance.

codes.notes: Professional ethics for state banking examiners.

codes.notes: Gold standard in investment ethics. 190,000+ charterholders globally.

codes.notes: Firm-level code. 1,500+ firms endorsed.

codes.notes: Required by SOX Section 406.

codes.notes: Fiduciary duty for all financial planning. ~95,000 certificants.

codes.notes: Overlaps with CFP Board. Client-first fiduciary standard.

codes.notes: Fee-only advisors' fiduciary oath. Members sign annually.

codes.notes: Alternative investment professionals.
~60,000 certified FRMs globally.
SRO for municipal securities.

codes.notes: SRO for futures and derivatives.

codes.notes: SEC-registered investment advisers. $35+ trillion AUM.
11th edition. Case studies interpreting the CFA Code.
UK-based. ~45,000 members.

codes.notes: Mutual fund and ETF governance.

codes.notes: Equity and fixed-income traders.

CIMA and CPWA certificants.

codes.notes: Model rules adopted by state securities regulators.

codes.document_title: Global Investment Performance Standards (GIPS) — Ethical Requirements
codes.notes: 1,700+ firms in 47 countries.

codes.document_title: Guide to Sound Practices for Hedge Fund Governance
codes.notes: Hedge fund governance. $2+ trillion AUM.

codes.notes: Model law for state adoption.
Adopted in all 50 states.
Nine canons for CPCU designation holders.

codes.organization: National Association of Insurance and Financial Advisors (NAIFA)
codes.notes: Largest insurance advisor association.
14 precepts. Enforced through disciplinary process.

codes.notes: Property-casualty actuaries.
Cross-practice code for all US actuaries.
125,000+ members globally.
Risk managers.
Health insurance agents and brokers.
CIP and FCIP designees.

codes.document_title: Insurance Core Principles — ICP 7 and ICP 8
codes.notes: 200+ jurisdictions.

codes.document_title: Code of Conduct and Ethics Policy
codes.notes: Mutual insurance companies.

codes.document_title: Standards of Professional Responsibility and Ethics
codes.notes: Trust and estate lawyers.

codes.notes: 140,000+ members.

PE fund investors. 600+ members, $2+ trillion.

codes.notes: DC plan fiduciaries.

codes.notes: ERISA fiduciary standards. Personal liability.

codes.notes: One of the oldest (1913). 17 Articles. ~1.5 million members.
Aspirational pledge supplementing Code of Ethics.
MAI and SRA designated appraisers.
Force of federal law via FIRREA 1989.

CPM and ARM designees. 12 articles.

codes.document_title: Code of Professional Standards and Ethics
codes.notes: Industrial and office real estate.
Apartment industry.

codes.notes: Invitation-only real estate advisors.
Retail real estate.

codes.notes: $300+ billion in licensed goods retail.
7,200+ member organizations, 185 countries.
733,000+ franchise establishments in US.

Foundation for legal ethics in all 50 states and DC. Adopted by ABA House of Delegates in 1983, continuously updated. Covers client-lawyer relationship, counselor, advocate, and professional responsibility. Enforceable through state bar associations.

codes.organization: American Institute of Certified Public Accountants (AICPA)
codes.notes: Effective December 15, 2014; revised annually on June 1. Covers integrity, objectivity, due care, competence, conflicts of interest, confidentiality, and public interest. All AICPA members required to adhere.

codes.document_title: Code of Ethics and Professional Conduct
codes.notes: Three tiers: Canons (broad principles), Ethical Standards (aspirational goals), and Rules of Conduct (mandatory, violation grounds for discipline). Enforced by National Ethics Council. Penalties include admonition, censure, suspension, or termination.

Available in French, German, Japanese, and Spanish. Includes fundamental canons, rules of practice, and professional obligations. Board of Ethical Review interprets dilemmas. PDF at nspe.org/sites/default/files/resources/pdfs/Ethics/CodeofEthics/NSPECodeofEthicsforEngineers.pdf

First adopted 1914, wholesale rewrite in 2020 using stakeholder model (replacing canon model). Principles: safe/resilient/sustainable infrastructure, respect/dignity/fairness, societal needs, quality of life.
Four fundamental principles: enhancement of human welfare, honesty/impartiality, competence/prestige, support of professional societies. Referenced in ASME By-Law B2.1.
Every applicant attests by signing membership application. Emphasis on paramount safety/health/welfare of public, environmental protection, and advising employers/clients of adverse consequences.

codes.organization: Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers (IEEE)
codes.notes: In existence since 1963 IEEE merger of AIEE and IRE. Every member agrees to abide by it upon joining. Violations reported via EthicsPoint hotline. Also has a separate Code of Conduct.

codes.document_title: Code of Ethics and Professional Conduct
codes.notes: Updated in 2018 (from 1992). Three sections: fundamental ethical principles, professional responsibilities, leadership responsibilities. Public good as primary consideration.

codes.organization: Institute of Management Consultants USA (IMC USA)
codes.notes: Condition of membership and CMC certification. Covers objectivity, fee basis, third-party commissions, reporting malfeasance. PDF at imcusa.org/wp-content/uploads/2023/02/imc_usa_code_of_ethics__final_.pdf

codes.organization: International Council of Management Consulting Institutes (ICMCI)
codes.notes: Global umbrella for CMC profession. Minimum ethical guidelines: confidentiality, realistic expectations, competence, financial disclosure. Re-certification every 3 years requires renewed pledge.

codes.document_title: The Chemical Professional's Code of Conduct
codes.notes: Evolved from 1965 Chemist's Creed through 1994 Chemist's Code of Conduct, updated 2007, 2012, 2016, 2019. Covers public health/safety, accurate records, sharing information, conflicts of interest.

codes.document_title: Ethical Principles of Psychologists and Code of Conduct
codes.notes: Five aspirational principles (beneficence/nonmaleficence, fidelity/responsibility, integrity, justice, respect) plus ten enforceable standards. Violations can lead to termination of membership or loss of licensure. Draft revision published Dec 2024.

codes.organization: American Association for the Advancement of Science (AAAS)
codes.document_title: Statement on Scientific Freedom and Responsibility
codes.notes: Adopted October 12, 2017 by AAAS Board. Links scientific freedom (inquiry, knowledge, communication) with responsibility (integrity, humanity, stewardship, human rights). Constitution amended in 1977 to include fostering scientific freedom and responsibility.

Core values: advocacy, honesty, expertise, independence, loyalty, fairness. Modified in 2000 to focus on education rather than enforcement. Members annually agree to follow as condition of membership.
Eight principles covering truth, substantiation, comparisons, bait advertising, guarantees/warranties, price claims, testimonials, good taste/public decency. Voluntary compliance.

Three core norms: do no harm, foster/maintain integrity, embrace ethical values (honesty, responsibility, equity, transparency, citizenship). Aspirational document. AMA also has separate Code of Conduct.

Three foundational principles: Stewardship (patient welfare, public/environment), Integrity (honesty/truthfulness), Respect (patients, clients, community). Comprises Principles, Code of Conduct, and Definitions. Violations subject to disciplinary action.

codes.document_title: Code of Ethics and Professional Conduct
codes.notes: Effective November 17, 2025. Four values: honesty, responsibility, respect, fairness. Both aspirational and mandatory standards. Applies to all PMI members, volunteers, certification holders and candidates. PDF at pmi.org/-/media/pmi/documents/public/pdf/ethics/pmi-code-of-ethics.pdf

For IT governance, audit, control, and security professionals. Covers due diligence, lawfulness, stakeholder interests, confidentiality, professional competence. Failure to comply can result in disciplinary measures.

First developed 1972, last modified 1989 for name change. Core principles: professional responsibility, professional development, ethical leadership, fairness and justice, conflicts of interest, use of information. Written by SHRM members with Ethics Resource Center.

Profession named in 1867. Canons contain Ethical Standards (aspirational goals) and objective Rules (enforceable). Covers duties to clients, employers, employees, other members. Also has separate Code of Environmental Ethics.
Companion to the Code of Professional Ethics, specifically addressing environmental stewardship responsibilities of landscape architects.

codes.organization: American Institute of Certified Planners (AICP) / American Planning Association
codes.document_title: AICP Code of Ethics and Professional Conduct
codes.notes: Originally adopted March 19, 2005; updated 2021. Three parts: aspirational principles (Section A), rules of practice and behavior (Section B, enforceable), enforcement procedures (Sections C-E). Violations can result in loss of AICP certification.

codes.document_title: Code of Ethics and Professional Conduct
codes.notes: Covers legal compliance, client relations (scope/fees/compensation disclosure), professional conduct, confidentiality, and intellectual property. Members may not seal/sign documents not prepared under their supervision.

For graphic/communication design professionals. Covers responsibilities to clients (correcting ethical violations), other designers (fair competition, no denigration), audiences, and society. Also publishes Design Business & Ethics handbook.

codes.document_title: Principles of Appraisal Practice and Code of Ethics
codes.notes: Covers appraisal of all property types (real estate, personal property, business, gems, machinery). Members must also follow USPAP. Requires independence, competency, accurate records kept 5 years, conflict disclosure.

Effective January 1, 2025 (latest revision). Specifically for real estate appraisers. Includes canons and enforceable ethical rules. Peer review system for enforcement. All designated members must comply.

codes.document_title: Code of Ethics and Standards of Practice
codes.notes: One of the first business ethics codes (adopted 1913). 17 articles covering duties to clients/customers, public, fellow REALTORS. 1.5M+ members. Training required every 3 years. Effective January 1, 2026.

codes.document_title: Code of Ethics and Standards of Professional Conduct
codes.notes: Effective January 1, 2024. 22 rules under 7 Standards: Professionalism, Integrity of Capital Markets, Duties to Clients, Duties to Employers, Investment Analysis, Conflicts of Interest, Member Responsibilities. Violations can result in revocation of CFA designation.

codes.organization: Society of Actuaries (SOA) / American Academy of Actuaries (AAA)
codes.notes: Jointly supported by five US actuarial organizations (Academy, ASEA, CAS, CCA, SOA). 14 precepts covering honesty, integrity, competence, conflicts of interest, confidentiality, public interest. Adopted October 15, 2000, effective January 1, 2001.

Mandatory guidance for internal audit profession. Four core principles: Integrity, Objectivity, Confidentiality, Competency. Applies to all IIA members, certification holders and candidates. Conformance required by International Standards.

codes.document_title: Standards of Professional Conduct and Code of Ethics
codes.notes: Three-fold responsibility: to clients (protect interests, advise against wrong conduct), to the member (maintain professional reputation), to government (comply with laws, timely/accurate tax filing). Must withdraw from returns if client insists on incorrect items.

codes.document_title: Code of Ethics and Professional Responsibility
codes.notes: Renamed from Code of Professional Conduct and Business Practices in November 2022. Core tenets: honesty/integrity, represent qualifications honestly, disclose conflicts of interest, abide by commitments/contracts.

Six principles: Legality, Honesty, Confidentiality, Quality, Fairness, Professionalism. Originally developed in the 1970s, formally established 1998. Connected by personal integrity and responsibility to clients and public.

codes.document_title: Code of Ethics for Consulting Engineers
codes.notes: Fundamental canons: paramount safety/health/welfare, perform in areas of competence, objectivity/truthfulness, act as faithful agents, avoid conflicts of interest, build professional reputation on merit.

36,000+ members across all industries. Core principles: fidelity/honesty/impartiality, respect/civility/non-discrimination, continuous improvement, competence, compliance with laws/standards, report unacceptable risk, avoid conflicts of interest.

codes.document_title: Code of Ethics and Standards of Practice for Environmental Professionals
codes.notes: Broad view of environment (physical, natural, cultural systems). Personally responsible for validity of data/analyses. Must not engage in dishonesty, fraud, deceit. No contingent fees conflicting with professional judgment. Recognized as public policy by NJ court.

Covers fair dealing (no manipulation/concealment/misrepresentation), professional standards, conflicts of interest disclosure, legal compliance (including non-discrimination), confidentiality. IFMA Board of Directors enforces.

codes.document_title: Code of Ethics and Standards of Conduct
codes.notes: Obligations to management (promote understanding of IT), fellow members (honesty/respect), society (disseminate knowledge, protect privacy/confidentiality), employers (faithful agents). Standards of Conduct expand on Code with specific behavioral rules.

Part of Policy Manual Section 8.7. Guides environmental professionals in balanced discharge of responsibilities to society, employers, clients, coworkers, subordinates, colleagues, and themselves. Ethics Committee provides training and awareness.

Maintains high standard of professional ethics in IP law practice. Provides advisory opinions on contemplated professional conduct. Regular membership requires conduct conforming to the Code per Board of Directors.

codes.document_title: Code of Ethics and Standards of Practice
codes.notes: Fair and honest dealing with landowners, industry associates, and public. Fiduciary duties. No undisclosed commissions/rebates. Accurate advertising. Professional land management (oil, gas, minerals, real estate).

CIPP certification requires agreement to IAPP Code of Ethics. Broader profession-wide code still under discussion. Challenges due to diversity of roles (technologists, lawyers, CPOs). Organization has 75,000+ members worldwide.

codes.document_title: Director Professionalism Statement and Code of Conduct
codes.notes: Premier membership organization for corporate board directors. Establishes standards for board oversight, fiduciary duty, governance best practices, conflicts of interest, and corporate stewardship.

codes.organization: Institute of Management Consultants USA (IMC USA)
codes.document_title: Code of Ethics (as applied to holding company management consulting)
codes.notes: Cross-listed from NAICS 541. Applies to management consultants advising holding companies and enterprise management. Covers objectivity, fee transparency, confidentiality.

Leading provider of organizational ethics research and best practices. Provides frameworks and benchmarking for corporate codes of conduct. Not a membership code per se but widely adopted as industry standard for holding companies.

codes.organization: Society of Corporate Secretaries and Governance Professionals
codes.notes: Professional association for corporate secretaries and governance professionals who support board-level decision-making. Ethics standards cover fiduciary duty, confidentiality, regulatory compliance, and stakeholder management.

codes.organization: CFA Institute (as applied to corporate treasury/investment management)
codes.document_title: Code of Ethics and Standards of Professional Conduct
codes.notes: Cross-listed from NAICS 541. Applies to investment professionals within holding companies managing subsidiary portfolios. 22 rules under 7 Standards.

sectors.sector_name: Administrative and Support and Waste Management and Remediation Services

codes.notes: Revised 2023 by global volunteer representatives. Six articles: lawful/ethical conduct, truthfulness/honesty/integrity, faithfulness/diligence, competence, confidentiality, no malicious injury to colleagues. Also adopted a separate Code of Conduct.
Companion to the Code of Ethics. Added by recommendation of global volunteer task force and approved by Global Board in 2023. More specific behavioral expectations.
Specific to ASIS certification holders (CPP, PCI, PSP). Additional professional conduct requirements beyond general membership Code of Ethics.

codes.document_title: Code of Ethics and Good Practices
codes.notes: Condition of ASA membership. Covers compliance with laws, ethical business operations, employer obligations (Social Security, unemployment insurance, workers comp), safe worksite assignments, employee protections. Separate codes for day labor and search/placement.

codes.document_title: Search and Placement Code of Ethics and Good Practices
codes.notes: Specialized code for executive search and permanent placement services within the staffing industry.

codes.document_title: Code of Ethics and Good Practices for Day Labor Services
codes.notes: Specialized code for day labor and construction labor staffing services.
Core values: integrity, encouragement, leadership, loyalty, professionalism, relevance, pride, connection, individual importance. For administrative professionals globally.

codes.organization: International Association of Professional Security Consultants (IAPSC)
codes.document_title: Certified Security Consultant Code of Ethics
codes.notes: Voluntary self-discipline above legal requirements. Specific provisions: confidentiality of client information, no advantage from inside information, no misrepresentation of qualifications, no contingent fees, neutrality in testimony.

12-point code standing for Integrity in Travel. Members must conduct business per the code. Duty to disclose material information affecting travel decisions. ASTA logo = symbol of professionalism and integrity. World's leading association of travel professionals.

codes.organization: Solid Waste Association of North America (SWANA)
codes.notes: Required for SWANA professional certification. Must be signed before certification application can proceed. 15,000+ members in solid waste management. Specific document available through certification materials.

For onsite wastewater recycling industry. Four pillars: legal compliance (local/state/national), honest/lawful competition, industry integrity over individual interests, faithful/honest representation with integrity and professionalism.

Cross-listed from NAICS 541. Part of Policy Manual Section 8.7. For environmental professionals in air quality and waste management. Ethics Committee provides training, papers, articles, and workshops.

11,000+ members. Four beliefs: public health/sanitation paramount, only high-quality merchandise/services, educate public on cleaning/sanitation, support scientific research. Violations subject to disciplinary provisions under Article III of ISSA Bylaws. Founded 1950.

codes.organization: Professional Background Screening Association (PBSA, formerly NAPBS)
codes.notes: Formerly National Association of Professional Background Screeners. Members discharge duties competently per applicable laws, adhere to moral/ethical standards, prevent improper disclosure. Ethics and Accreditation committee establishes technology and security standards.

Adopted 1975. Two core principles: obligations to students and obligations to the profession. Addresses non-discrimination, academic freedom, confidentiality. Foundational code for American public education.
Adopted by AFT Executive Council October 2018, updated July 2023. Governs member conduct and organizational representation. AFT also endorsed the MCEE.

Originally adopted 1966, revised 1987 and 2009. Addresses responsibilities to the discipline, students, colleagues, institution, and civic society. Foundational document for academic ethics and faculty governance.

codes.organization: National Association for the Education of Young Children (NAEYC)
codes.document_title: Code of Ethical Conduct and Statement of Commitment
codes.notes: Adopted 1989, updated 2005, reaffirmed 2011. Four sections: relationships with children, families, colleagues, and community/society. Accompanied by Statement of Commitment. Core document for early childhood education professionals.

codes.organization: National Association of State Directors of Teacher Education and Certification (NASDTEC)
codes.document_title: Model Code of Ethics for Educators (MCEE)
codes.notes: 2nd edition July 2023. Five principles: responsibility to the profession, professional competence, responsibility to students, responsibility to the school community, responsible/ethical use of technology. Developed collaboratively with NEA, AFT, and other organizations. Overseen by NCAEE.

First adopted 1974, revised 1984, 1992, 1997, 2000, and 2020. Four themes: respecting dignity/rights, professional competence, honesty/integrity, responsibility to schools/families/communities/profession/society. 17 ethical principles. Effective July 2020.

codes.document_title: ASCA Ethical Standards for School Counselors
codes.notes: Developed collaboratively with practitioners and counselor educators across the nation. Covers Pre-K through 12. Addresses student rights, confidentiality, cultural sensitivity, gender identity, and professional responsibilities. Revised 2010, 2016.

codes.organization: NASPA — Student Affairs Administrators in Higher Education
codes.document_title: NASPA Guiding Principles and Code of Ethics
codes.notes: Adapted from Higher Education Consortium for Student Affairs Certification Code of Ethics. Three parts: guiding principles, aspirational goals, and ethical obligations. Eight guiding principles including integrity, inclusivity, equity, and continuous learning.

codes.organization: Council for the Advancement of Standards in Higher Education (CAS)
codes.document_title: CAS Statement of Shared Ethical Principles
codes.notes: Seven shared ethical principles: autonomy, non-malfeasance, beneficence, justice, fidelity, veracity, and affiliation. Not intended to replace individual association codes but articulates shared foundational principles across student services professions.

codes.organization: International Association of Universities (IAU) / Magna Charta Observatory (MCO)
codes.document_title: IAU-MCO Guidelines for an Institutional Code of Ethics in Higher Education
codes.notes: Approved at 14th IAU General Conference 2012. Provides comprehensive guidelines for universities to develop or review institutional codes of ethics. Developed after 2010 IAU International Conference on Values and Ethics in Vilnius.

Based on ANA Center for Ethics and Human Rights. Core values: child well-being, diversity/equity/inclusion, excellence, innovation, integrity, leadership, scholarship. Updated 2024. Covers school nursing practice including advocacy, dignity, equity, and competency.

codes.document_title: Recommendation on Education for Peace, Human Rights and Sustainable Development
codes.notes: Adopted November 2023 by UNESCO's 194 Member States. 14 guiding principles including ethic of care, compassion, solidarity, and global citizenship. Non-binding guidance for reshaping education systems. Replaces 1974 Recommendation.

First adopted 1847, continuously updated. Nine Principles of Medical Ethics. The most comprehensive professional medical ethics code in the US. Includes opinions organized by chapter covering patient-physician relationships, consent, privacy, genetics, organ transplantation, research, and more.

Nine aspirational principles adopted 1957, revised 1980, 2001. Separate from the full Code of Medical Ethics. Defines honorable behavior standards for physicians including competence, honesty, respect for law, continuing education, and community service.

codes.document_title: ADA Principles of Ethics and Code of Professional Conduct
codes.notes: Three components: Principles of Ethics (aspirational), Code of Professional Conduct (enforceable rules), and Advisory Opinions. Five fundamental principles: patient autonomy, nonmaleficence, beneficence, justice, veracity. Binding on ADA members; violations may result in discipline.

Established 1852, most recently revised 1994. Eight principles covering covenantal patient-pharmacist relationship, patient care, autonomy, dignity, justice, competence, individual and community health, and professional obligations.

codes.document_title: Ethical Principles of Psychologists and Code of Conduct
codes.notes: First published 1953, current version 2002 with 2010 and 2017 amendments. Five aspirational principles: beneficence/nonmaleficence, fidelity/responsibility, integrity, justice, respect for rights/dignity. Ten enforceable ethical standards. Under revision as of 2024.

Current version 2014. Six foundational principles: autonomy, nonmaleficence, beneficence, justice, fidelity, veracity. Covers client welfare, professional responsibilities, confidentiality, informed consent, diversity, technology in counseling, research, and supervision.

codes.document_title: Code of Ethics for the Physical Therapy Profession
codes.notes: New combined Code effective Jan 1, 2026, adopted at 2025 House of Delegates. Merges prior PT Code and PTA Standards. Eight core values: accountability, altruism, collaboration, compassion, duty, excellence, integrity, social responsibility.

codes.document_title: AOTA 2025 Occupational Therapy Code of Ethics
codes.notes: First established 1975. Current 2025 edition; reviewed every 5 years. Seven Core Values: Altruism, Equality, Freedom, Justice, Dignity, Truth, Prudence. Used by some states in licensure acts. Addresses emerging technologies and evolving healthcare landscape.

First implemented 1952, current version 2016 (revised from 2010). Partly obligatory/disciplinary and partly aspirational. At least 1 of 30 continuing education hours per 3-year cycle must be in ethics. Covers speech-language pathology and audiology.

codes.document_title: AOA Code of Ethics and Standards of Professional Conduct
codes.notes: Code of Ethics (2007) sets forth basic tenets; Standards of Professional Conduct (adopted June 2011) amplifies the Code. Also includes the Optometric Oath (revised 2021). Covers referral, confidentiality, access to care, competence, and professional relationships.

Ratified by ACA House of Delegates 2023. Seven principles covering excellence/best practices, professional conduct, patient-centered care, doctor-patient relationships, confidentiality, collaboration with other health professionals, and education/training.

codes.document_title: Guidelines for Ethical Conduct for the PA Profession
codes.notes: Code adopted 1983, amended 1985, reaffirmed 1990. Ethical Guidelines for Professional Conduct updated July 2021. Core tenets: patient autonomy, beneficence, nonmaleficence, justice, diversity, confidentiality, and competence.

codes.document_title: AAMA Code of Ethics and Creed
codes.notes: Two components: Code of Ethics (professional principles) and AAMA Creed (aspirational pledge). Code addresses dignity, confidentiality, honor, continuous improvement. Creed: dedication to care and well-being of all people, loyalty, confidence.

codes.document_title: Code of Ethics for Emergency Physicians
codes.notes: Approved 1997, revised 2008, 2016, 2017, and October 2023. Recognizes unique challenges of emergency medicine. Covers autonomy, beneficence, non-maleficence, justice, confidentiality, and physician role in society. Includes Policy Compendium.

codes.document_title: The Principles of Medical Ethics With Annotations Especially Applicable to Psychiatry
codes.notes: First published 1973. Based on AMA Principles of Medical Ethics with psychiatry-specific annotations. Includes the Goldwater Rule (Section 7.3) prohibiting public diagnosis of non-patients. Ethics Committee provides guidance, education, and handles complaints.

First published 1984, current Seventh Edition published January 2019. Updated every 5-7 years. Covers precision medicine, genetic testing, research, telemedicine, EHR, social media, and end-of-life care. Published in Annals of Internal Medicine. Foundation for ACP policy.

codes.organization: American Association of Marriage and Family Therapists (AAMFT)
codes.notes: Revised Code effective January 1, 2026. Core values: inclusive environment, equity, belonging, diversity, integrity, innovation. Ethical standards are enforceable by AAMFT Ethics Committee. Covers systemic and relational therapies.

Updated May 2023. 114 ethical standards in six areas: professional responsibilities, counseling relationships, supervision/consultation, testing/appraisal/research, counselor education, and telemental health/social media/technology. Applicable to all NBCC certificants.

codes.organization: NAADAC — The Association for Addiction Professionals
codes.notes: Updated 2021 and 2025. Accepted standard of practice for NAADAC members and NCC AP certified addiction professionals. Covers confidentiality, professional conduct, credentials, non-discrimination, and ethical decision-making in behavioral health.

Covers all AHIMA members and non-member certification holders. Principles address consumer privacy, confidentiality, service before self-interest, professional honor, compliance with policies, and advocacy. Also includes Standards of Ethical Coding.

codes.organization: American Society of Radiologic Technologists (ASRT) / American Registry of Radiologic Technologists (ARRT)
codes.notes: Joint code by ASRT and ARRT. Covers professional conduct, service to humanity, non-discrimination, radiation safety, patient privacy/confidentiality, competence, and collaboration. ARRT separately publishes enforceable Standards of Ethics.

codes.organization: American Society for Clinical Laboratory Science (ASCLS)
codes.notes: Three core duties: duty to patient, duty to colleagues and the profession, duty to society. Addresses non-discrimination, confidentiality, competence, equitable distribution of healthcare resources. Laboratory professionals as patient advocates.

codes.document_title: Code of Ethics for the Certified Registered Nurse Anesthetist
codes.notes: Establishes ethical standards for the nurse anesthesia profession. Under revision in 2026. Covers confidentiality, patient rights, informed consent, malpractice insurance, public welfare, and collaboration. Applies to all CRNA practice roles.

codes.document_title: ACNM Code of Ethics with Explanatory Statements
codes.notes: Describes moral obligations guiding midwifery behaviors. Emphasizes respect for basic human rights, dignity, autonomy, justice, confidentiality, accountability, and advocacy for women's rights in healthcare.

codes.document_title: AARC Statement of Ethics and Professional Conduct
codes.notes: Sets standards for respiratory therapists. Core provisions: integrity, evidence-based practice, continuing education, patient rights (privacy, informed consent, refusal of treatment), non-discrimination, and avoidance of conflicts of interest.

Revised May 2022. Five shared professional values: Caring & Compassion, Integrity, Respect, Competence, Accountability. Covers equitable treatment, regulatory compliance, ethical conduct, appropriate relationships, and patient safety.

codes.organization: Academy of Nutrition and Dietetics / Commission on Dietetic Registration (CDR)
codes.document_title: Code of Ethics for the Nutrition and Dietetics Profession
codes.notes: Updated effective June 2018. Based on four principles: autonomy, non-maleficence, beneficence, justice. Applicable to RDNs and NDTRs. Addresses digital health, social media, and technology. Enforced through disciplinary process.

Patient welfare and rights above all other considerations. Covers competence, referral obligations, informed consent, confidentiality, and professional conduct across all aspects of podiatric professional life.

codes.organization: National Association of Emergency Medical Technicians (NAEMT)
codes.document_title: Code of Ethics for EMS Practitioners
codes.notes: Written by Dr. Charles B. Gillespie, adopted 1978, revised June 2013. Pledges to conserve life, alleviate suffering, promote health, do no harm. Updated to be more patient-centered and includes social media provisions.

Original 2002 Principles of the Ethical Practice of Public Health. Updated November 2019. Uses social justice and social determinants of health as framing tools. Includes decision-making framework for difficult choices.

Adopted 1948 as modern successor to the Hippocratic Oath. Revised 2017 and renamed 'The Physician's Pledge.' Key additions: patient autonomy and dignity, physician self-care, collegial respect. First amendment in decades.

Adopted 1949 as complement to Declaration of Geneva. Amended 1968, 1983, and most recently revised 2022. Defines duties of physicians toward patients, other professionals, themselves, and society. Canon of ethical principles for worldwide medical profession.

codes.document_title: The ICN Code of Ethics for Nurses
codes.notes: First adopted 1953, most recently revised 2021. Four principal elements providing framework for ethical conduct. Reflects lessons from COVID-19 pandemic. Model for national nursing ethics standards globally.

codes.document_title: International Principles of Ethics for the Dental Profession
codes.notes: Updated 2018. Guidelines for every dentist covering patient care, competence, responsibility for treatment, continuing education, and professional conduct. Supplemented by FDI Dental Ethics Manual (1st edition 2007). FDI represents 1M+ dentists worldwide.

codes.document_title: FIP Statement of Professional Standards — Code of Ethics for Pharmacists
codes.notes: Approved by FIP Council 2014. Framework for national pharmacy codes of ethics. Based on bioethical principles: respect for autonomy, beneficence, non-maleficence, justice. Applies to all pharmacist practice settings including non-clinical roles.

codes.document_title: Ethical Principles and Responsibilities of Physiotherapists and Member Organisations
codes.notes: First ratified 1959, updated 2019, current version 2023. Eight ethical principles covering patient rights, legal compliance, professional autonomy, competence, equitable/inclusive services. Expects member organisations to publish and promote their own codes.

codes.document_title: WPA Code of Ethics for Psychiatry
codes.notes: Adopted October 2020 by WPA General Assembly, superseding the 1996 Declaration of Madrid. Four sections: clinical practice, psychiatric education, psychiatric research, and public/mental health promotion. Drafted over nearly a decade with worldwide input.

codes.document_title: The Patient Care Partnership: Understanding Expectations, Rights, and Responsibilities
codes.notes: Evolved from AHA Patient's Bill of Rights (1973, revised 1992). Establishes patient rights including treatment decisions, advance directives, privacy, confidentiality, dispute resolution, and quality care. Key ethical framework for hospital care.

Amended November 2017. Standards for healthcare executives covering professional relationships with colleagues, patients, organizations, community, and society. Adherence is a membership requirement. Includes Ethics Self-Assessment tool and Ethics Toolkit.

codes.document_title: Statements on Principles (including Code of Professional Conduct)
codes.notes: Founded 1913 with resolution on honest practice and prohibition of fee splitting. Includes Code of Professional Conduct, Qualifications of Surgeons, and surgeon-patient relationship. Also includes Guidelines for Ethical Use of Social Media by Surgeons.

codes.document_title: Patient Rights and Organizational Ethics Standards
codes.notes: Ethics standard first included in 1992 Accreditation Manual for Hospitals. Requires ethics education and mechanisms to address ethical issues. Covers patient rights, advance directives, cultural competency, non-discrimination, and safe environments. Accreditation exceeds legal minimums.

codes.organization: American College of Health Care Administrators (ACHCA)
codes.notes: Founded 1962. Code preserves highest standards of integrity for long-term health care administrators. Covers non-discrimination, competence, confidentiality, compliance with laws/regulations, quality of care, and continuing education.

codes.organization: Association of Professional Chaplains (APC) / Association for Clinical Pastoral Education (ACPE) / Others
codes.document_title: Common Code of Ethics for Chaplains, Pastoral Counselors, Pastoral Educators, and Students
codes.notes: Affirmed November 2004 by six organizations as unified code for spiritual care professionals. Covers non-discrimination, integrity and welfare of those served, confidentiality, credentials, competence, and abuse of power. Applies to chaplains serving in nursing and residential care settings.

First approved 1960, most substantive revision 1996, updated 2017. Four sections: Preamble, Purpose, Ethical Principles, Ethical Standards. Six core values: service, social justice, dignity/worth, importance of human relationships, integrity, competence. Used by licensing boards, courts, insurers.

codes.document_title: Code of Ethics for Nurses with Interpretive Statements
codes.notes: First adopted 1950. Latest 2025 revision: 10 provisions (new 10th provision on environmental and global well-being). Over 6,000 nurses contributed input; 49 experts refined it. Addresses health disparities, racism, workplace safety, emerging technologies. Cornerstone of ethical nursing practice.

codes.document_title: AAP Code of Conduct and Bioethics Policy Statements
codes.notes: Committee on Bioethics established 1979. Publishes policy statements on pediatric bioethical issues including informed consent, parental permission, end-of-life care, religious objections, and research involving children. Code of Conduct addresses professional interactions.

codes.document_title: Global Social Work Statement of Ethical Principles
codes.notes: Approved at General Meeting July 2018 in Dublin (replacing 2004 Statement). Joint with IASSW. Principles of social justice, human rights, collective responsibility, and respect for diversities. Applies to all contexts of social work practice, education, research, and digital technology/social media.

Revised 2015, further revision proposed 2024. Three foundational principles: Stewardship, Integrity, Respect. Code of Conduct includes: competent care, patient welfare, professionalism. Violation may result in AVMA disciplinary action. Relevant to animal welfare services in social assistance settings.

subsectors.name: Performing Arts, Spectator Sports, and Related Industries

codes.organization: SAG-AFTRA (Screen Actors Guild - American Federation of Television and Radio Artists)
codes.notes: Union code governing member conduct. Updated post-#MeToo. Covers workplace harassment, professional behavior, and solidarity obligations. Also issued separate Code of Ethics for Talent Managers.

codes.document_title: Standards and Protocols for the Use of Intimacy Coordinators
codes.notes: February 2024 update formalizing consent, safety, and professionalism protocols for scenes involving nudity or simulated intimacy.

codes.document_title: Codes, Guidelines and Internal Membership Rules
codes.notes: Union for professional actors and stage managers in live theater. Covers member obligations re punctuality, professional conduct, dispute resolution via Deputies and Business Representatives.
Covers 7,800+ managers of arenas, stadiums, performing arts centers, convention centers, and amphitheaters. Required affirmation for CVE/CVP certification.
Article 10 of NCAA Constitution covers ethical conduct in college athletics: honesty, sportsmanship, anti-gambling, reporting violations.

codes.organization: North American Society for Sport Management (NASSM)
codes.notes: Academic and professional body for sport management. Covers research integrity, professional competence, and social responsibility in sport.
Governs athletes, coaches, officials, and staff. Strong SafeSport provisions on abuse, harassment, and athlete welfare.

subsectors.name: Museums, Historical Sites, and Similar Institutions

codes.notes: Adopted 1993, revised 2000. Fundamental to AAM accreditation. Covers governance, collections stewardship, public trust, and institutional integrity. All museums regardless of size expected to follow.

codes.document_title: ICOM Code of Ethics for Museums
codes.notes: Global standard adopted 1986, revised 2004. 8 principles covering institutional governance, acquisition, due diligence for provenance, cultural property protection, community engagement. Translated into 38 languages.
Required for AZA accreditation. Covers animal welfare, conservation mission, honest communication, and ethical treatment of wildlife. AZA accredits 240+ facilities.

codes.document_title: SAA Core Values Statement and Code of Ethics
codes.notes: Covers archival professionals at museums, historical sites, and cultural institutions. Emphasizes access, accountability, diversity, preservation, and responsible custody.

codes.organization: Association of Registrars and Collections Specialists (ARCS)
codes.notes: Ethics for museum registrars and collections managers handling acquisitions, loans, and de-accessions. Covers fiduciary duty, provenance research, and conflict of interest.

Updated regularly (2026 version published Dec 2025). Member companies pledge responsible gaming in daily operations. Covers underage gambling prevention, self-exclusion, employee training, and advertising ethics.

codes.document_title: Responsible Marketing Code for Sports Wagering
codes.notes: Specific code for sports betting advertising and marketing. Covers truthfulness, targeting restrictions, and responsible messaging.

codes.organization: International Association of Amusement Parks and Attractions (IAAPA)
codes.notes: Global attractions industry. Covers quality products/services, fact-based communications, truthful advertising, conflict of interest avoidance, social and environmental responsibility.
Code of conduct for Certified Park and Recreation Professionals (CPRP). Covers ethical standards for parks, recreation, and leisure services professionals.

codes.document_title: NIGC Regulations — Minimum Internal Control Standards
codes.notes: Federal regulatory standards for tribal gaming operations. Includes ethical conduct provisions for gaming employees, anti-fraud measures, and integrity of gaming operations.

codes.document_title: AHLA Safe Stay Guidelines and Ethics Standards
codes.notes: Industry guidelines covering employee conduct, anti-trafficking measures, and guest safety. AHLA also maintains the 5-Star Promise on employee safety and anti-harassment. Specific ethics code not publicly posted as standalone document.

codes.organization: International Hotel & Restaurant Association (IH&RA) / International Hospitality Institute
codes.document_title: Code of Ethics for the Hospitality Industry
codes.notes: Global hospitality ethics framework. Covers guest safety, employee welfare, environmental sustainability, and fair business practices. IH&RA represents hotels in 150+ countries.
Covers financial and technology professionals in hospitality. Addresses integrity, competence, confidentiality, and professional objectivity for hotel finance/IT staff.

codes.document_title: ServSafe Food Handler Ethical Standards and Event Code of Conduct
codes.notes: The NRA does not publish a standalone industry-wide code of ethics but maintains ServSafe certification standards for food safety and an event code of conduct. Historical 1930s 'Code of Fair Competition' established early ethical expectations.
Covers manufacturers, importers, distributors, and retailers of specialty foods. Mandates honest advertising, fair dealing, respect for competitors and customers.
Ethics code for restaurant facility management professionals. Covers professional integrity, competence, and responsible facility stewardship.
Covers Certified Dietary Managers and foodservice professionals in institutional settings (hospitals, schools, care facilities). Focuses on food safety, nutrition integrity, and client welfare.

codes.organization: National Institute for Automotive Service Excellence (ASE)
codes.notes: All ASE-certified technicians pledge to uphold this code. Covers first-class workmanship, lifelong learning, customer welfare, recommending only necessary work, and maintaining public respect for the profession. Embedded in ASE certification process.
HVAC contractors. Covers honest representation, fair pricing, quality workmanship, environmental responsibility, and continuing education.
Covers electronics technicians and certified professionals in repair and maintenance of electronic equipment. Emphasizes honesty, competence, and fair dealing.
While primarily construction, covers remodeling and home repair/maintenance. Covers quality workmanship, fair dealing, compliance with building codes, and customer satisfaction.

Professional code for licensed barbers. Covers sanitation, client confidentiality, professional competence, and community responsibility. Part of the American Barber Certification Council (ABCC) program.

Binding on NFDA members. Covers obligations to family, care of decedent, public, government, and NFDA. Violations subject to disciplinary action. Addresses pricing transparency and pre-need arrangements.

codes.organization: National Association of Productivity and Organizing Professionals (NAPO)
codes.notes: Professional organizers and productivity consultants. Covers client confidentiality, competence, integrity, reasonable fees, and professional boundaries.

codes.organization: International Cemetery, Cremation and Funeral Association (ICCFA)
codes.notes: Covers cemetery, cremation, and funeral service professionals internationally. Emphasizes dignity, transparency in pricing, and respect for diverse cultural and religious practices.

codes.organization: National Association of Professional Pet Sitters (NAPPS)
codes.notes: All NAPPS members must adhere to a code of ethics covering animal welfare, client confidentiality, professionalism, and responsible pet care.

subsectors.name: Religious, Grantmaking, Civic, Professional, and Similar Organizations

codes.notes: Board approved December 2023, now enforceable. All AFP members required to sign. Covers donor rights, stewardship, solicitation ethics, and fiduciary responsibility. 26 specific standards.

codes.document_title: Statement of Values and Code of Ethics for Nonprofit and Philanthropic Organizations
codes.notes: Foundational ethics framework for the nonprofit sector. Covers public good commitment, accountability beyond the law, responsible stewardship, openness, inclusiveness, and fundraising ethics.

codes.organization: Standards for Excellence Institute / Independent Sector
codes.document_title: Standards for Excellence: An Ethics and Accountability Code for the Nonprofit Sector
codes.notes: Comprehensive ethics and accountability code. 6 categories: Mission/Strategy, Leadership, Ethics/Legal, Finance/Operations, Resource Development, Public Awareness. Online self-assessment available.

codes.document_title: Ethics and Accountability for Nonprofits — Principles and Standards
codes.notes: Compiles ethical standards from state associations of nonprofits. Covers governance, financial transparency, donor stewardship, and organizational accountability.

codes.document_title: ASAE Standards of Conduct — Core Ethical Standards
codes.notes: Governs conduct for leaders of professional and trade associations. Covers basic conduct, confidentiality, competition, giving/receiving, and member relations. Updated September 2022.

codes.document_title: Principles and Practices for Effective Grantmaking
codes.notes: Ethical framework for foundations and grantmaking organizations. Covers donor intent, effective governance, transparency, responsible investment, and legal compliance.

7 standards for evangelical Christian nonprofit organizations. Covers doctrinal commitment, governance, financial oversight, truthful communication, and responsible stewardship. 2,600+ accredited members.

codes.document_title: Nonprofit Board Member Codes of Conduct and Ethics
codes.notes: Model code for nonprofit board governance. Covers fiduciary duty, conflict of interest, confidentiality, duty of care, and board member accountability.

codes.document_title: INA Recommended Practices — Code of Ethical Conduct
codes.notes: Covers professional nannies. Addresses child welfare, confidentiality, professional development, family/employer relationships, and ethical boundaries. INA Credentialed Nanny designation.

codes.document_title: Domestic Workers Bill of Rights — Ethical Standards Framework
codes.notes: Framework for fair and ethical treatment of household workers (nannies, house cleaners, caregivers). Covers fair wages, safe working conditions, freedom from harassment, and privacy. Adopted as law in 10+ states.

subsectors.name: Executive, Legislative, and Other General Government Support

codes.document_title: Standards of Ethical Conduct for Employees of the Executive Branch
codes.notes: 5 CFR Part 2635. Binding federal regulation. Based on Executive Order 12731 (1990). Modernization updates published May 2024. Covers gifts, conflicts of interest, outside employment, misuse of position. Applies to all 2M+ executive branch employees.

8 principles: advance public interest, uphold Constitution, promote democratic participation, strengthen social equity, fully inform, demonstrate personal integrity, promote ethical organizations, advance professional excellence. Ethics Implementation Committee since 2014.

codes.document_title: ICMA Code of Ethics with Guidelines
codes.notes: Adopted 1924 — among the oldest professional ethics codes in public administration. 12 tenets covering democratic government, public trust, political neutrality, equity, transparency, and professional development. ICMA enforces through ethics investigations.
Model code for county officials. Covers public trust, impartiality, transparency, proper use of public resources, and avoiding conflicts of interest.

codes.organization: United Nations — International Civil Service Commission (ICSC)
codes.document_title: Standards of Conduct for the International Civil Service
codes.notes: Applies to all UN system employees. Replaces 1954/2001 editions. Covers independence, impartiality, integrity, accountability, respect for diversity, non-discrimination, and conflicts of interest. Translated into 6 official UN languages.
Covers government finance officers in the US and Canada. Addresses honest financial management, transparency, prudent use of public funds, avoiding conflicts of interest, and professional competence.

codes.document_title: Code of Ethics for City Officials
codes.notes: Model ethics code for municipal elected and appointed officials. Covers public trust, transparency, conflict of interest, impartiality, and proper use of public office.

subsectors.name: Justice, Public Order, and Safety Activities

codes.organization: International Association of Chiefs of Police (IACP)
codes.notes: Originally adopted 1957 at 64th IACP Conference, updated 2024. Foundational document for law enforcement worldwide. Covers primary duty to serve, confidentiality, use of force, impartiality, and personal conduct. Widely adopted by US police departments.

codes.organization: International Association of Chiefs of Police (IACP)
codes.notes: Short-form ethical pledge for law enforcement. Emphasizes integrity, bravery, honor, and treating all persons with dignity and respect. Part of IACP Ethics Toolkit.

codes.document_title: Fire Service Professional Code of Ethics
codes.notes: Covers fire service leadership. Establishes criteria encouraging personnel to promote a culture of ethical integrity and high standards of professionalism. Separate Firefighter Code of Ethics also maintained.

codes.organization: National Fire Protection Association (NFPA) / National Fallen Firefighters Foundation
codes.notes: Joint initiative. Covers all fire service personnel. Addresses integrity, accountability, leadership, professional competence, community service, and personal conduct on and off duty.

Covers corrections professionals. Requires honesty, respect for dignity of individuals, commitment to professional service, protection of civil/legal rights, and reporting corrupt or unethical behavior.

codes.document_title: Code of Ethics for Jail Officers
codes.notes: Specific to jail officers. Covers duty as good citizens, professional conduct, respect for incarcerated persons' rights, and commitment to community.

codes.document_title: Code of Ethics for the Field of Community Corrections
codes.notes: Covers probation, parole, and community corrections officers. Addresses public safety, offender rehabilitation, professional integrity, and fair administration of justice.

codes.document_title: IAEM Code of Ethics and Professional Conduct
codes.notes: Covers emergency management professionals (CEM/AEM certified). Addresses public safety, professional competence, ethical decision-making in crisis, and cooperation across agencies.

4th edition. Chapter 1 covers ethical obligations of prosecutors: duty to seek justice not merely convict, disclosure obligations, avoiding conflicts, and professional conduct. Supplements ABA Model Rules.

codes.organization: National Association of State Workforce Agencies (NASWA)
codes.document_title: NASWA Code of Ethics and Professional Standards
codes.notes: Covers state-level administrators of unemployment insurance, employment services, and workforce development programs. Emphasis on equitable service delivery, data privacy, and program integrity.

While primarily covering professional social workers (NAICS 62), directly relevant to public administration of human services programs. Covers service, social justice, dignity, human relationships, integrity, and competence. 155 standards in 6 sections.

codes.organization: International Public Management Association for Human Resources (IPMA-HR)
codes.notes: Covers public sector HR professionals administering civil service, benefits, and employment programs. Addresses merit-based systems, non-discrimination, confidentiality, and professional development.

codes.document_title: NEHA Member Code of Ethics / Credential Code of Ethics
codes.notes: Covers environmental health professionals (sanitarians, health inspectors). Separate credential code for REHS/RS holders. Covers continuing education, public health protection, and professional integrity.

codes.document_title: NAEP Code of Ethics and Standards of Practice
codes.notes: Covers environmental impact assessment professionals, NEPA practitioners, and environmental compliance officers in government. Covers scientific integrity, transparency, and public interest.

codes.organization: Institute of Environmental Management and Assessment (IEMA)
codes.notes: International body for environmental and sustainability professionals. Covers professional competence, ethical decision-making, environmental stewardship, and public interest. 15,000+ members in 100+ countries.

subsectors.name: Administration of Housing Programs, Urban Planning, and Community Development

codes.organization: American Institute of Certified Planners (AICP) / American Planning Association (APA)
codes.document_title: AICP Code of Ethics and Professional Conduct
codes.notes: Adopted 2005, revised 2021. Three-part structure: aspirational principles (all planners), rules of conduct (AICP members), and enforcement procedures. Covers social justice, expanding choice and opportunity, racial and economic integration.

codes.organization: National Association of Housing and Redevelopment Officials (NAHRO)
codes.document_title: NAHRO Code of Professional Conduct and Ethics
codes.notes: Covers professionals in public housing, community development, and housing redevelopment agencies. Addresses fair housing, tenant welfare, transparency, and proper use of public funds.
Covers building code enforcement officers in housing and urban development. Addresses impartial enforcement, due process, professional competence, and public safety.
Covers economic development professionals. Addresses integrity, honesty, public trust, professional competence, and responsible development. Enforcement procedures in place.
Also listed under 925. Primary code for economic development professionals. Members pledge integrity, objectivity, and bringing respect to the profession.

All AAPC members required to sign annually. Sets standards for campaign and business practices to promote integrity and confidence in the political system. Relevant to government economic program administration.

codes.organization: Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD)
codes.notes: Framework for government integrity in economic program administration. 13 principles covering commitment, responsibilities, strategic approach, standards, merit-based employment, and risk management. Adopted by 38 OECD member countries.

codes.document_title: NASA Ethics Program — Standards of Ethical Conduct
codes.notes: NASA employees subject to 5 CFR Part 2635 (government-wide) plus 5 CFR Part 6901 (NASA-specific supplemental standards). Covers outside employment approval, financial disclosure, contractor relations, and scientific integrity.

codes.document_title: NASA Supplemental Standards of Ethical Conduct
codes.notes: 5 CFR Part 6901. Agency-specific regulations supplementing OGE standards. Requires prior approval for outside employment and addresses NASA-specific conflicts of interest.

codes.document_title: Guidelines for Promoting Scientific and Research Integrity
codes.notes: Covers scientific misconduct, research data integrity, peer review ethics, and responsible authorship. Applies to all NASA-funded research.

Updated May 2024. Comprehensive ethics regulation for all DoD military and civilian personnel. Covers gifts, outside activities, financial interests, post-government employment, political activities, and standards of conduct.

codes.document_title: Code of Conduct for Members of the Armed Forces of the United States
codes.notes: Executive Order 10631 (1955), amended by EO 12633 (1988). 6 articles covering duty, surrender, captivity, and resistance. Applies to all US military personnel at all times. Foundational military ethics document.

codes.organization: United Nations — International Civil Service Commission (ICSC)
codes.document_title: Standards of Conduct for the International Civil Service
codes.notes: Also listed under 921. Applies to UN personnel in peacekeeping, international security, and diplomatic roles. Covers independence, impartiality, integrity, and conduct during international operations.

codes.document_title: CIA Values — Ethics and Integrity Standards
codes.notes: CIA's stated values include Service, Integrity, Excellence, Courage, Teamwork, and Stewardship. Subject to Intelligence Community Directive 120 on intelligence community ethics. Detailed internal ethics code not publicly released.

codes.document_title: Principles of Professional Ethics for the Intelligence Community
codes.notes: Issued by the Director of National Intelligence. Covers all 18 US intelligence agencies. Addresses mission integrity, truth, lawfulness, objectivity, accountability, and stewardship. Classified annexes supplement the public document.

cross_sector_codes.notes: Nine core principles based on ILO conventions. 90 member companies. Widely adopted across wholesale and retail supply chains.

cross_sector_codes.document_title: amfori BSCI Code of Conduct v.2021
cross_sector_codes.notes: 13 Performance Areas. Recognized by Consumer Goods Forum SSCI. Used by major retailers and wholesalers globally.
Originally electronics-focused, now covers retail, auto, and toy companies. Five sections covering Labor, Health & Safety, Environment, Ethics, Management Systems.
Ten Principles of Fair Labor. Applies across apparel, footwear, and general merchandise supply chains for both wholesale and retail.
